summary: Appeal under TADA Act against acquittal in kidnapping and murder case; challenge to rejection of confessional statements of three accused; admissibility of confessions under TADA s.15 and procedural compliance; issue estoppel incorrect basis for rejecting Salim Zargar's confession; co-accused confessions rejected due to procedural flaws; prosecution failed to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt; appellate review of evidence; reliability of witnesses questioned.
legal_provisions_cited: Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987 s.3
Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987 s.4
Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987 s.15
final_judgment: Appeal dismissed; acquittal by Special Court upheld; confessional statements rightly excluded due to procedural irregularities; no sufficient evidence to overturn benefit of doubt.
